LESSON: SIGN READING 3.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Sign reading 3.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign reading 3.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: How do we tell where events have taken place in a story? 2. How do we identify characters in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign reading 3.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner articulates signs effectively as they discuss the setting of a story with peers.

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner makes connections as they use the five-finger model to retell as they sign the content of the story in a few

words.

Values:
Respect: acceptance is enhanced as the learner accepts diverse opinions from peers during discussion.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: self-esteem developed as the learner creatively retells a story.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Comprehension skills emphasized in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources

Assistive devices fitted with appropriate technology such as Hearing aids and amplifiers, charts showing words with the target letter sounds, flash

cards showing words with target letter sound, signed audio-visual recordings, print or digital stories, pocket charts, print and digital flash cards
